q: Which animal says 'quack'?
x: Ducks say quack quack!

q: Which animal has a long neck?
x: A giraffe's long neck helps it eat leaves from tall trees.

q: Which one is a fruit?
x: Bananas grow on banana plants.

q: What do we use to walk?
x: We walk and run with our feet.

q: What falls from clouds when it rains?
x: Rain is water falling from the clouds.

q: Which baby animal is a chick?
x: A chick hatches from an egg.

q: Which one flies in the sky?
x: Airplanes fly high in the sky.

q: How do we feel when we get a hug?
x: Hugs help us feel safe and loved.

q: The sun is hot.
x: The sun is a giant ball of hot gas.

q: Fish can walk on land.
x: Fish live in water and swim with their fins.

q: Which animal hops and has a pouch?
x: Mother kangaroos carry their babies in a pouch.

q: Where does a bee live?
x: Bees live together in a hive.

q: What do we taste with?
x: Our tongue tells us if food is sweet, salty or sour.

q: What do plants need to grow?
x: Plants need water, sunlight and air to grow.

q: When do we see the moon and stars?
x: We see the moon and stars best at night.

q: Which food comes from a cow?
x: Cows give us milk.

q: Which one goes on train tracks?
x: Trains run on long metal tracks.

q: Who puts out fires?
x: Firefighters put out fires and help keep people safe.

q: A cat has four legs.
x: Cats walk on four legs.

q: Snow is hot.
x: Snow is frozen water, so it is cold.

q: We should brush our teeth every day.
x: Brushing keeps our teeth strong and clean.

q: Carrots grow under the ground.
x: The orange part of a carrot is a root that grows in the soil.

q: Which animal sleeps all winter?
x: Some bears sleep for most of the winter. This is called hibernation.

q: How many legs does a bird have?
x: Birds have two legs and two wings.

q: What do we call a group of stars that makes a picture?
x: People long ago named star pictures like the Big Dipper.

q: Which season comes after summer?
x: Spring, summer, autumn, winter, and then spring again.

q: What helps protect our brain?
x: The skull is a hard bone around the brain.

q: Who teaches children at school?
x: Teachers help children learn new things.

q: How many wheels does a bicycle have?
x: 'Bi' means two: a bicycle has two wheels.

q: Which is the biggest?
x: Mountains can be thousands of meters tall.

q: Penguins can fly.
x: Penguins cannot fly, but they are great swimmers.

q: The moon gives off its own light.
x: The moon shines because sunlight bounces off it.

q: A seed can grow into a plant.
x: With water, soil and sun, a seed sprouts and grows.

q: Our heart pumps blood.
x: Your heart pumps blood all around your body.

q: Which animal is a mammal?
x: Dolphins breathe air and feed their babies milk, so they are mammals.

q: What does a caterpillar turn into?
x: A caterpillar makes a chrysalis and comes out as a butterfly.

q: Which planet do we live on?
x: Earth is the only planet we know that has life.

q: What happens to ice when it gets warm?
x: Warm ice melts and becomes water.

q: How many days are in a week?
x: Monday to Sunday: seven days.

q: Which ocean is the biggest?
x: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.

q: Which food is made from milk?
x: Yogurt, cheese and butter are made from milk.

q: Your friend falls down. What can you do?
x: Helping others shows kindness.

q: Spiders are insects.
x: Spiders have 8 legs. Insects have 6, so spiders are not insects.

q: The Earth goes around the Sun.
x: It takes Earth one year to go around the Sun.

q: A magnet can pick up a paper clip.
x: Magnets pull things made of iron, like paper clips.

q: Deserts get a lot of rain.
x: Deserts are very dry places with little rain.

q: Which animal is a reptile?
x: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin. Frogs are amphibians and bats are mammals.

q: How many bones does a grown-up have?
x: An adult skeleton has 206 bones.

q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
x: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

q: What do we call water when it turns into a gas?
x: When water boils, it turns into steam, a gas.

q: What is the hot liquid rock inside a volcano?
x: Hot melted rock inside a volcano is magma. Outside, it is called lava.

q: How many minutes are in one hour?
x: One hour has 60 minutes.

q: What do we call a person who studies the stars?
x: Astronomers use telescopes to study space.

q: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
x: Roots drink water and hold the plant in the ground.

q: Frogs start life as tadpoles in water.
x: Tadpoles slowly grow legs and become frogs.

q: The Sun is a star.
x: The Sun is the star closest to Earth.

q: Sound can travel through water.
x: Whales talk to each other with sounds that travel far through water.

q: The North Pole is very hot.
x: The North Pole is covered in ice and is very cold.

q: What force pulls things down to the ground?
x: Gravity pulls everything toward the Earth.

q: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
x: Herbivores, like cows and rabbits, eat only plants.

q: Which planet has the biggest rings?
x: Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock.

q: Which organ helps us breathe?
x: Our lungs take in oxygen from the air.

q: What is the longest river in the world?
x: The Nile in Africa is usually called the longest river.

q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
x: A hexagon has six sides, like a honeycomb cell.

q: How many months are in a year?
x: A year has 12 months, from January to December.

q: What should you do before crossing the street?
x: Stop, look left and right, then cross with a grown-up.

q: Plants make their own food using sunlight.
x: This is called photosynthesis.

q: Bats are birds.
x: Bats are mammals. They feed their babies milk.

q: Mars is called the red planet.
x: Rusty dust makes Mars look red.

q: Most of the Earth is covered by water.
x: About 70 out of every 100 parts of Earth's surface is water.

q: What are the three states of matter?
x: Ice is a solid, water is a liquid and steam is a gas.

q: Which animal is the largest on Earth?
x: The blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived.

q: What causes day and night?
x: Earth spins once a day. The side facing the Sun has day.

q: What carries oxygen around your body?
x: Red blood cells carry oxygen to every part of the body.

q: Which is the largest continent?
x: Asia is the biggest continent and has the most people.

q: What is 7 × 8?
Sound travels faster than light.
x: Light is much faster. That is why we see lightning before we hear thunder.

q: An octopus has three hearts.
x: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.

q: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level.
x: Everest is about 8,849 meters tall.

q: Your heart is a muscle.
x: The heart is a strong muscle that never stops working.

q: What gas do plants take in from the air?
x: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.

q: How long does it take the Moon to go around the Earth?
x: The Moon circles Earth about once every 27 days.

q: What do we call a scientist who studies rocks?
x: Geologists study rocks, soil and how the Earth changes.

q: Why do some birds fly south in winter?
x: This long trip is called migration.

q: What is 3/4 of 100?
Which invention lets us talk to people far away?
x: Alexander Graham Bell got the first patent for the telephone in 1876.

q: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
x: At sea level, water boils at 100 °C.

q: Jupiter is the smallest planet.
x: Jupiter is the biggest planet. Mercury is the smallest.

q: Which part of a cell holds its instructions (DNA)?
x: The nucleus is the control center of the cell.

q: What are the big moving pieces of the Earth's crust called?
x: When plates move, they can cause earthquakes and build mountains.

q: What is a light-year?
o: How far light goes in a year
x: A light-year is a distance: about 9.5 trillion kilometers.

q: What is 15% of 200?
x: 10% of 200 is 20 and 5% is 10, so 15% is 30.

q: Electricity can flow easily through copper.
x: Copper is a good conductor, so wires are often made of it.

q: All bacteria are harmful.
x: Many bacteria are helpful, like the ones in our gut and in yogurt.

q: What is the chemical symbol for water?
x: Water has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

q: Which layer of the atmosphere protects us from harmful sun rays?
x: The ozone layer blocks much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet light.

q: What is at the center of our solar system?
x: All the planets orbit the Sun.

q: Why do we recycle?
x: Recycling turns old things into new ones and saves materials and energy.

q: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
x: Sunlight travels about 150 million kilometers in about 8 minutes.

q: The skin is the largest organ of the human body.
x: Skin covers and protects your whole body.
